title: Iron Graph — Fitness Tracking & Analytics App
description: Production-grade Flutter mobile application for serious lifters and strength athletes. Detailed workout logging, routine management, personal record tracking, and data-driven analytics through interactive charts and heatmaps.
challenge: Fitness apps on the market either oversimplify tracking (missing granular set/rep/weight data) or overwhelm users with complexity. The challenge was building an app that provides deep analytics — recovery heatmaps, weekly volume vs. hypertrophy targets, progression trends, and PR detection — while keeping the workout logging experience fast and frictionless. Additionally, the app needed to work fully offline, persist active workouts across app kills, handle complex data aggregation efficiently (single-pass queries across thousands of sets), and deliver a polished UX with animations and haptic feedback on a mobile-first responsive layout.
solution: Feature-based Flutter architecture with clean separation: DAOs for data encapsulation, Freezed models for immutability, and Riverpod providers for reactive state management. Implemented Drift/SQLite with 8 schema migration versions for a robust local-first database seeded with 250+ hypertrophy exercises. Built a real-time active workout system that persists state to SharedPreferences and recovers seamlessly on restart. Created a multi-chart analytics dashboard using fl_chart (bar, line, donut, heatmaps) powered by single-pass join queries. Added an animated rest timer with a depleting ring animation, color transitions, and vibration feedback. Designed a responsive layout supporting mobile (bottom nav) and tablet (navigation rail) with custom fading tab transitions.
impact: Fully functional, offline-capable fitness app with 7+ screens, 4 analytics chart types, 22,000+ exercises, and a complete workout lifecycle (create routine → log sets → view summary → track PRs → analyze trends). Performance optimizations (KeepAlive tabs, RepaintBoundary on charts, lazy queries, debounced search) ensure smooth 60fps interactions even with large datasets.
